subtopic: Pheromone traps for yellow stem borer
information: Install pheromone traps at 20 traps per hectare, about 20 days after transplanting, to mass-trap male moths. Lures contain 10-15 mg pheromone.
After harvest, flood the fields thoroughly and plough with discs or rotators to kill hibernating stem borer larvae.
Pest:defender ratio of 2:1 may help avoid spraying against planthoppers, since natural enemies can keep numbers in check.

Chemicals are a last resort, used only when pest populations cross the economic threshold level (ETL). Brown planthopper ETL: 10-15 hoppers per hill from early to late tillering; 15-20 per hill from panicle initiation to booting.

Insect pests: pink bollworm, cotton bollworm, spotted bollworm, jassid, whitefly, aphid, thrips, mealybugs, mirids, tobacco caterpillar, stem weevil. Diseases: root rot, Fusarium wilt, boll rots, target spot, leaf spots, cotton rust, grey mildew, bacterial leaf blight, cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD), tobacco streak virus. Nematodes: root-knot and reniform.
At 45 days after sowing (DAS), install pheromone traps at 5 per hectare for pink bollworm monitoring.

subtopic: Seed treatment for early sucking pests
information: Commercial seeds are coated with systemic insecticides such as Imidacloprid 70 WS or Thiamethoxam 30 FS, giving early protection against sucking pests (0-60 DAS).
verification_note: Verify label rates before any dosing content

information: Avoid broad-spectrum sprays (guide: do not apply synthetic pyrethroids or organophosphates) to prevent whitefly resurgence during 0-60 DAS.
Between 61 and 90 DAS, observe for rosette flowers (a sign of pink bollworm larvae), pluck and destroy them.
Do not extend the cotton crop beyond 180 days, to prevent late-season pest build-up.
